steps.label: Plan and Build Your Own Game
steps.content:
Year 6 Scratch

Plan and Build Your Own Game

Year 6, 6.2.5

  • Plan a game: sprites, controls, variables, and how it ends.
  • Build it from the plan, testing each piece as you add it.
  • Check it has the parts every good game needs.

steps.label: A Plan Before Code
steps.content:
A Plan Before Code

Here is the plan for Fruit Catcher, the catching game you have built. Yours will have the same parts.

Fruit Catcher plan

  • Sprites: Bowl (the player moves it), Apple (falls from a random place).
  • Controls: left and right arrow keys.
  • Variables: score (apples caught), lives (misses left, starts at 3).
  • Win or lose: lose when lives reaches 0.
  • A plan lets you, or someone else, build the game without guessing.
  • Each line of the plan becomes a script or a sprite.
  • Build one line at a time and test it before the next.

steps.label: Check: The Plan
steps.content:
Check: The Plan

Use the Fruit Catcher plan.

items.prompt: In the Fruit Catcher plan, what is lives?
items.explain: lives stores a number that changes while the game runs, so it is a variable.

items.prompt: You add 6 new blocks at once and the game breaks. Why is testing after each small change better?
options: You know the bug is in the part you just added
items.explain: Testing each small change means a new bug must be in the few blocks you just added.

steps.label: Activity 1: Build Your Game
steps.content:
Activity 1: Build Your Game

Work on your own, from your plan. Build one piece, test it, then the next.

Build it

  • Sprites first, then the controls.
  • Then a loop that keeps the game running.
  • Then a variable: set it at the green flag, change it during the game.
  • Then an if block that decides something, and a way to win or lose.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.label: Make It Better: A Second Level
steps.content:
Make It Better: A Second Level

When every check passes, add a level with a broadcast and a backdrop, as in Level Up.

if <(score) = (10)> then
broadcast [level up v]
end

when I receive [level up v]
switch backdrop to [Level 2 v]
  • Add a second backdrop for level 2.
  • Broadcast a message when the player reaches your target.
  • Make level 2 harder: faster enemies, or a new sprite.
  • The bonus check in My Game looks for the second level.

steps.label: Activity 2: Level Two
steps.content:
Activity 2: Level Two

Work on your own. Open My Game again: your project is still there.

Build it

  • Add a second backdrop.
  • Switch to it with a broadcast when the player reaches your target.
  • Make level 2 harder than level 1.
  • Press Check my project to see the bonus check go green.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.
